p.seg: De harmonica consideratione Boetius ita disseruit:
quia neque solum in terminis speculationem proportionis habet, neque solum in differentiis, sed in utrisque communiter.
Quaerit enim ut quemadmodum sunt ad se extremi termini, sic majoris ad medium differentia contra differentiam medietatis ad ultimum.
Concerning the harmonic relationship, Boethius stated it was so [called]
"because it is concerned with a proportion not only between the terms, and not only between their differences, but between both together.
It requires that just as the extreme terms are to each other, so too is the difference between the larger term and the mean and between the mean and the lesser term.
Ipsarum quoque musicarum consonantiarum, quas symphonias nominant, proportiones in hac pene sola medietati frequenter invenies.
Namque symphonia diatessaron, quae princeps et quodammodo vim obtinet elementi, in ejusmodi harmonicis medietatibus invenitur.
You will often find the proportions of those very consonances that they call symphonies in this virtually unique mean.
For the interval of the diatessaron, which is primary and has an elemental force in a way, is found in harmonic means of this kind.
Ut sunt VI. ad VIII. sint ergo hujusmodi medietatis termini, quorum extremi sint dupli, et alii quorum extremi tripli sint, ita:

figure.desc: VI. | VIII. | XII || IV. | VI. | XII.

p.seg: Duodenarius igitur ad senarium duplus est;
et in alia dispositione XII. ad IV. triplus est.
Horum si differentias colligamus et ad se invicem comparemus, epitrita proportio, idem diatessaron symphonia colligitur.
Inter VI. enim et XII. senarius est, et inter IV. et XII. octonarius;
qui scilicet octonarius ad senariu sesquitertiam efficit proportionem.
Just as 6 is to 8, therefore let there be terms for means of this type whose extremes are double, and others whose extremes are triple, thus:
12, therefore, is double the 6,
and in the other arrangement 12 to 4 is triple.
If we take the differences of these and compare them in turn to each other, a proportion of 4:3, that is, a diatessaron, is formed.
For between 6 and 12 is a 6, and between 4 and 12 an 8
which makes a proportion of 4:3 in relation to the 6.
In eadem quoque medietate et diapente symphonia componitur.
In duplici, videlicet XII. ad VIII., et in triplici, videlicet VI. ad IV. sesquialtera.
Moreover, in the same mean a diapente is formed.
In the duple, 12 to 8, and in the triple, 6 to 4, there is obviously a sesquialtera proportion.
Post hunc autem diapason consonantia est, ut IVI ad XII.
In triplici quoque dispositione simul diapente et diapason symphonia componitur, ut sunt VI. VIIII. XVIII.
After this, however, there is a diapason consonance, as [for example] 6 to 12.
In the triple disposition, moreover, the consonance of both a diapente and diapason is formed, as in 6:9:18.
Et quoniam triplus duas continet consonantias, diapente scilicet ac diapason, in differentiis ejusdem triplicis eumdem triplum reperiemus.
Nam inter VI. et VIIII. ternarius differentia est, et inter VIIII. et XVIIII. novenarius, qui ad ternarium triplus est.
And since the triple proportion contains two consonances, namely the diapente and the diapason, we shall discover the same triple relationship in the differences of these same triple proportions,
for between 6 and 9 the difference is three, and between 9 and 18 nine, which is three times three."
In dupla vero proportione, major terminus differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est,
et rursus minor terminus ad differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est.
Nam inter VIII. et XII. quaternarius est, qui ad eundem duodenarium triplus est, et inter VI. et VIII. binarius, qui rursus ad eundem senarium triplus est.
